profile_md:
## Buckman (Buckman Laboratories International) - Investor Profile

**Overview.** Buckman is a Memphis-based, vertically integrated specialty chemical maker. It started in 1945 with microbial control (biocides) for pulp and paper, and that is still its core. Its own descriptions list three main markets: pulp & paper, leather and water treatment, plus process chemistry for oil & gas, biofuels/ethanol, sugar, power, metalworking, coatings, plastics, wood and agriculture. Bluntly, Buckman is **not a pure water treatment company**. It is a paper and leather process-chemicals business with a sizeable industrial water treatment line (cooling, boiler, raw water, process water, reuse and wastewater). We estimate water treatment at about a quarter of sales.

**History & ownership.** Dr. Stanley J. Buckman founded the company in Memphis in 1945 with a single 55-gallon reactor making BSM-11. It expanded early: Canada in 1948, the Cadet, Missouri plant and Mexico in 1963, Belgium in 1964, and South Africa, Brazil and Australia from 1971. The family holding company is Bulab Holdings, Inc., set up in 1987. Leadership passed from Stanley to Robert (Bob) Buckman, then to Steven Buckman and Katherine Buckman Gibson. Junai Maharaj has been CEO since 2017. On March 3, 2025 Pritzker Private Capital (PPC), the Chicago family-direct-investing firm, signed a deal to buy Buckman. PPC is investing alongside Buckman family members and management, and the deal closed on July 1, 2025. Advisors were Evercore (company sell-side), Houlihan Lokey (for a select family shareholder) and McMillan LLP (Canadian counsel to PPC). No terms were disclosed. PPC named strategic acquisitions as a growth lever. One trade-press article said the seller was "Peninsula Pacific Strategic Partners". It looks AI-generated, and every primary release says Buckman was family-owned, so we disregard that claim.

**Products & chemistries.** Buckman makes most of its active chemistry itself in Memphis and Cadet. Its product lines are:
- Busan-branded biocides and microbial control agents, including organosulfur fungicides and preservatives.
- Oxamine (EPA Green Chemistry award 2012) and Maximyze enzymes for recycled fiber/papermaking (Green Chemistry award 2004 lineage).
- Ionene and other polymers for water treatment and papermaking.
- Retention, drainage and strength additives, and deposit control.
- Leather tanning and beamhouse chemicals.
- Cooling and boiler inhibitor programs.
- Digital dosing and monitoring. The 2017 CiDRA Chemical Management acquisition brought the ECHOWISE entrained-air measurement technology.

It operates about 6 manufacturing hubs (2025 deal release). Older company material says 10 manufacturing sites worldwide.

**End markets & customers.** The largest end market is paper, board and packaging recycling mills. There, Buckman sells both process chemistry and the mills' water programs. Next come leather tanneries (a global niche where Buckman is a leading supplier), then industrial water treatment for ethanol plants, oil & gas, power/utilities and sugar, then metalworking fluids, coatings/plastics preservation and agricultural uses. In 2017 Buckman sold its eastern-Canada general water treatment book to Klenzoid (Triwater), covering cooling/boiler water for manufacturing, food & beverage, institutional and power customers. The stated aim was to focus on "oil/gas, ethanol, utilities, paper and leather". That tells you Buckman's water business is industrial and tied to its process verticals, not a broad commercial/institutional service route like Nalco, ChemTreat or the regional independents.

**Footprint.** Headquarters, a manufacturing complex and the new $10 million Robert H. Buckman Chemical R&D Pilot Plant (opened December 2024) are at 1256 N. McLean Blvd., Memphis, TN. The second US plant is at 14664 E. Highway 47, Cadet, MO. Abroad, Buckman has operations or plants in Canada, Mexico, Belgium (Ghent), Brazil (Sumaré), South Africa, Australia, Singapore, China (Shanghai) and India. It sells in 90+ countries. In August 2025 it formed Atul-Buckman, a joint venture with Atul Ltd, to make and sell water treatment chemicals in India and Sri Lanka.

**Financials.** Buckman has never published audited financials.
- **Revenue:** Company history material from about 2020 says "sales of more than $500 million" with 1,500 associates. Since then there were price increases (5-9% in North America and APAC in late 2024, 5-12% in EMEA paper, a US tariff surcharge in 2025), while headcount fell to ">1,300" at the 2025 deal. We **estimate 2024 revenue at about $600M** (range $550-700M).
- **EBITDA:** Not disclosed. At an assumed 16% margin, typical for a biocide-heavy specialty mid-cap, it would be about **$95M**. Treat this as an estimate only.
- **Water share:** Water treatment is roughly 25% of sales (about $150M). The US may be ~45% of that, giving **US water treatment revenue of about $68M** (range $55-90M).

**M&A strategy.** Historically Buckman made few deals: Eclipse Chemical (Canada water treatment, 2001) and CiDRA Chemical Management (2017), plus the 2017 divestiture in eastern Canada. Under PPC, expect a buy-and-build approach, likely in water treatment and digital monitoring. No add-ons had been announced as of September 2026. The only post-close move found is the Atul joint venture.

**Competitive position.** In paper Buckman competes with Solenis (including Diversey), Kemira and Ecolab/Nalco, and in leather with Stahl, TFL and LANXESS. In industrial water it faces Ecolab, Veolia, ChemTreat, Solenis and Kurita. Its strengths are in-house biocide chemistry and regulatory registrations, deep niche application know-how, and customer intimacy.

**Risks.**
- Structural decline in graphic paper.
- Concentration in leather.
- EPA/FIFRA and EU BPR biocide re-registration costs.
- Exposure to raw material and tariff swings.
- Sub-scale position in US water against much larger programs.
- New private equity ownership and any leverage it brings. No credit rating was found, which points to private or club debt.

**Uncertainties.** Revenue, EBITDA, the segment split and the US share are all estimates. Deal EV and financing are undisclosed.
